finding.claim: The embed domain allowlist validates the host with PHP parse_url(), but the URL that is actually fetched is the raw string, which the embed/embed library and curl parse differently. A URL such as https://evil.example\@allowed.com/ is read by parse_url() as user="evil.example\", host="allowed.com" and passes the filter. A WHATWG-style or curl parser treats the backslash as a path separator and requests evil.example. This is a parser differential that can bypass the allowlist and cause SSRF or embedding of an untrusted origin. I did not run the downstream fetch, so the end-to-end exploitability is unconfirmed.
finding.source: Markdown author text on a line of its own, parsed as an Embed block by EmbedStartParser. The URL is attacker-controlled and kept verbatim by EmbedParser.
finding.sink: OscaroteroEmbedAdapter::updateEmbeds() calls embedLib->getMulti(urls) and server-side fetches the URL. The returned HTML is then emitted unescaped by EmbedRenderer::render().

trace.note: The raw URL is stored in the Embed node with no normalization.
The adapter, which is the DomainFilteringAdapter when configured, receives the embed list.
parse_url() extracts the scheme, then the host at line 51. The backslash and userinfo quirk makes the host allowed.com.
The host equality or suffix match passes, so the embed is kept.
The original, unnormalized URL string is fetched.
The remote-supplied embed HTML is output raw.

finding.guards_checked: Scheme check for http/https only (lines 44-49). Trailing-dot strip and lowercase on the host. Suffix match uses '.'.$domain, so evil-allowed.com is not accepted. EmbedProcessor replaces non-top-level embeds with plain text. None of these rejects backslashes, userinfo, or a host that differs between parsers. The check is not applied to the normalized URL that is fetched.
